title: The Writing on the Wall
backstory: God once humbled proud Nebuchadnezzar, driving him out among the beasts until he knew that the most high God rules in the kingdom of men (Daniel 5:20-21). His son Belshazzar has not learned it. At a great feast for a thousand of his lords he calls for the golden vessels his father took from the temple in Jerusalem, and they all drink out of them (Daniel 5:1-3). In that same hour, fingers of a man's hand come out and begin to write on the wall of the palace (Daniel 5:5).

passages.synopsis: King Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his lords. He called for the golden cups taken from God's temple in Jerusalem, and they drank from them while praising idols of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone. Suddenly the fingers of a man's hand appeared, writing on the palace wall. The king's face went pale and his knees knocked together, and none of his wise men could read the writing.

The queen came in and remembered a man in the kingdom in whom, she said, was the spirit of the holy gods — Daniel, who had explained dreams for Nebuchadnezzar long ago. So Daniel was brought in before Belshazzar. The king promised him scarlet clothing, a chain of gold, and third place in the kingdom if he could read the writing. The old servant of God stood before the proud king.

Daniel told the king to keep his gifts, but said he would read the writing. He reminded Belshazzar how God had humbled mighty Nebuchadnezzar until he knew that the most high God rules in the kingdoms of men. Belshazzar knew all this, yet he did not humble his heart. He lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven and praised gods that cannot see or hear. So the hand was sent from God.

Daniel read the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. God had numbered the days of Belshazzar's kingdom, weighed the king in the balances and found him wanting, and would give the kingdom to the Medes and Persians. Belshazzar kept his promise and honored Daniel. That very night the kingdom was taken from him, and Darius the Median began to rule.

triviaQuestions.question: What did King Belshazzar see during his great feast?
options: Fingers of a man's hand writing on the wall
triviaQuestions.explanation: Daniel 5:5 — "In the same hour came forth fingers of a man’s hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king’s palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote."

triviaQuestions.question: What was the writing on the wall?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Daniel 5:25 — "And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN."

triviaQuestions.question: What did TEKEL mean?
options: You are weighed in the balances and found wanting
triviaQuestions.explanation: Daniel 5:27 — "TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting."

triviaQuestions.question: Who took the kingdom that very night?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Daniel 5:31 — "And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old."

reflection: Belshazzar knew what God had done for Nebuchadnezzar, yet he did not humble his heart. What would it look like for you to stay humble before God this week?
